books.author: Eleanor Harte
books.title: Whisper of Stones
books.description:
A storm took Mairi Macrae. Seventy years later, the island is still keeping her secrets.

When Mara Thompson arrives at Craigmuir Hall, she wants only a position quiet enough to let her disappear. Hired as companion and reader to the formidable Isobel Fraser, Mara expects letters, household accounts, and the ordinary duties of a respectable post.

But Craigmuir is no ordinary house.

Perched above a narrow Scottish channel, the Hall holds the memory of a vanished young woman, a silver thistle brooch, and a lie that has shaped the island for generations. The village says Mairi Macrae ran away before the storm. Thomas Sinclair never believed it. And now, seventy years later, Mara begins to understand that some stories survive because someone powerful needed them to.

Ewan Macrae has spent his life holding Craigmuir, the pier, and the island together by force of will. He has no time for mysteries, no patience for old grief, and no intention of letting a guarded stranger disturb what little order remains. Yet Mara sees what others miss, and the closer they come to the truth, the harder it becomes to keep their distance.

As the island’s past rises through letters, stones, and silence, Mara and Ewan must decide whether exposing the truth will free Craigmuir—or destroy what is left of it.

Atmospheric, romantic, and quietly suspenseful, Whisper of Stones is a Scottish historical romance about buried secrets, inherited sorrow, and the courage it takes to choose love after a lifetime of fear.

books.author: Eleanor Harte
books.title: The Glove Shop on Market Lane
books.description:
She spent a lifetime helping other people build their futures. Now she must risk everything to claim one of her own.

After years in devoted service, Mollie Martin leaves behind the safety of Penharrow and purchases a struggling glove shop on Market Lane in the bustling Cornish port of Penzance. For the first time in her life, every success and every failure will belong to her alone.

The shop offers more than gloves. Every customer brings a story hidden in the hands they extend across the counter—new marriages, quiet grief, family secrets, and ambitions carefully concealed beneath polished manners. Mollie soon discovers that selling gloves means learning far more about people than she ever expected.

Yet the business she has purchased carries mysteries of its own. The previous owner departed in haste, leaving behind ledgers that do not quite balance, a locked cabinet no one wishes to discuss, and questions that others seem reluctant to answer. Even Jory Nance, the reserved carpenter helping repair the aging shop, appears to know more than he is willing to say.

As friendships deepen, old secrets surface, and unexpected affection begins to challenge the fiercely independent life she has worked so hard to build, Mollie must decide whether true freedom means standing entirely alone—or learning whom she can finally trust.

Set against the rugged coast of Victorian Cornwall, The Glove Shop on Market Lane is a richly atmospheric historical romance about second chances, quiet courage, and the belief that the life worth claiming is the one you choose for yourself.

books.author: J Leme Thompson
books.title: The Cotton Boll Queen
books.description:
Before there was Belle Devereaux, there was Annabelle.

Named for a poem, Annabelle Lee Crump knows the weight of being watched.

In the cotton fields outside Yazoo City, Mississippi, she has learned to make herself invisible — hiding her beauty, intelligence, and ambition behind purple-streaked hair and chipped black polish. The land is patient. The men are possessive. And visibility, she learns early, is not a blessing. It is an invitation.

When Celeste Voss, a woman of quiet power and exacting control, stops at the gas station where Annabelle works the night shift and asks a question no one has ever asked her — have you ever thought of leaving? — Annabelle understands the question is really an offer.

She takes it.

New York City becomes her education. As Belle Devereaux, she learns how power moves through rooms, how silence can be placement, and how a woman who controls her own visibility controls almost everything else. Under Celeste’s guidance she is translated, not transformed. The girl from Mississippi does not disappear. She is reorganized — like a violin in a Braque painting, taken apart and reassembled according to different rules.

The women she works beside are extraordinary in their own right: precise, observant, fluent in the language of rooms most people never learn to read. Together they build a world with its own rules.

Until it doesn’t hold.

When a man of extraordinary patience and dangerous curiosity decides Belle is exactly what he has been looking for — not for desire alone, but for possession — she discovers that the most sophisticated trap is the one that looks like an opportunity.

And Mississippi, it turns out, does not let go easily.

The Cotton Boll Queen is a novel about reinvention, survival, and the cost of becoming valuable. Moving from the cotton fields of Mississippi to the penthouses of Manhattan, it is the story of a woman who builds herself from almost nothing — and refuses to belong to anyone but herself.

books.author: J LemeThompson
books.title: Everything's Jake
books.description:
In Elmwood, Tennessee, everyone knows everyone.

Faith is steady. Land is inherited. Reputations are earned slowly and kept carefully. When a man like Tom Reeves—attorney, scoutmaster, deacon, the judge's son—takes an interest in your boy, you feel grateful. You feel seen.

John Robinson is fighting to save his family's farm. Sarah Robinson knows something is wrong with her son but cannot name it. Jake is eleven years old, eager to belong, and learning that being chosen by the right people feels like opportunity.

It isn't.

Everything's Jake is a novel about the slow architecture of trust—how it is built, how it is used, and what it costs when the wrong person holds it.

Set against the quiet rhythms of rural Tennessee, it examines how ordinary goodness can coexist with extraordinary harm, and how the institutions we rely on to protect us sometimes protect only themselves.

In small communities, trust moves faster than doubt. And not all guidance reveals its cost at once.

books.title: The Durable Physique
books.description: A practical guide to building and maintaining strength, muscle, and resilience for the long term.

books.author: August Rowan
books.title: Under Scrutiny
books.description: When the Capitol's digital security is breached from the inside, Ethan Hayes has minutes to stop his own system being turned against him.

books.author: August Rowan
books.title: The Sentinel Protocol
books.description: A retired intelligence officer. A list that should not exist. A message through a channel that was supposed to be dead.

books.author: Eleanor Harte
books.title: The Willowbrook Bargain
books.description:
At Willowbrook Manor, duty has a price.
Henrietta Beaumont has been raised to understand what is expected of her: obedience, composure, and a suitable marriage. With her family’s Cornish estate slipping toward ruin, that suitable marriage has become urgent. Lord Alistair Finch is wealthy, well-connected, and willing to rescue Willowbrook — if Henrietta becomes his wife.

But Finch’s generosity feels less like courtship than possession.

When Henrietta meets Julian Thorne, a disgraced bookseller with a ruined family name and a dangerous connection to Finch’s past, she begins to uncover the truth beneath Willowbrook’s polished surfaces. Old debts, altered ledgers, family silence, and buried betrayals suggest that her marriage is not merely a solution to financial trouble. It is part of a bargain arranged long before she understood the terms.

As pressure tightens around her, Henrietta must decide whether duty will bind her to a life chosen by others — or whether love, courage, and the truth can unmake the bargain made in her name.

The Willowbrook Bargain is a richly atmospheric Victorian historical romance of inheritance, scandal, coercion, and hard-won love on the windswept Cornish coast.
